Q: Apply different function to each leaf of pytree in `jax` A:

I discovered jax.tree.map (which has a syntax more powerful than I expected) and the following works like a charm:

data_pytree = (5, (5, 5))
func_pytree = (f0, (f10, f11))
map_fn = lambda a, b: b(a)
jax.tree.map(map_fn, data_pytree, func_pytree)

With jax.tree.map_with_path, it's possible to be even more fine grained.

Q: Codename One Maven: Simulator loads theme/images but Android APK uses default theme — correct location for theme.res and images? A:

src/main/resources is the only place for resources (such as a res file). What can hide your file is the name "theme.res" since maven projects always use a css file that would generate a theme.res too which will probably override your theme.

The solution would be to rename your pre-existing file to myTheme and then in the code fix the theme loading to load myTheme instead of theme.

Q: how can you tell if a replace operator was successful A:

As a fun exercise, what would I do if ReferenceEquals wasn't an option?

I think it comes down to whether the replacing text is the same length the replaced text. If they are different, you can just check the Length property.

If they are the same, we'd potentially need to traverse the entire 100 Mb string. That seems less than ideal... and so I might implement my replace method. Given I know both the target and new text are the same length, I can make assumptions not available to the regular method. For example, I could use .Net's String.Create() API to allocate the exact size buffer I need, and then do the substitutions in-place, at near the same speed as a single traversal. Then I could track for myself whether any substitutions were made.

Q: How can I encode the filename parameter of Content-Disposition header in HTTP? A:

  • There isn’t any interoperable way to encode non-ASCII names in Content-Disposition. Browser compatibility is a mess.

  • The theoretically correct syntax for use of UTF-8 in Content-Disposition is very weird: filename*=UTF-8''foo%c3%a4 (yes, that's an asterisk, and no quotes except an empty single quote in the middle)

  • This header is kind of-not-quite-standard (HTTP/1.1 specification acknowledges its existence, but it doesn't require clients to support it).

There is a simple and very robust alternative: use a URL that contains the filename you want.

When the name after the last slash is the one you want, you don't need any extra headers!

This trick works:

/real_script.php/fake_filename.doc

And if your server supports URL rewriting (e.g., mod_rewrite in Apache) then you can fully hide the script part.

Characters in URLs should be in UTF-8, percent-encoding byte-by-byte:

/mot%C3%B6rhead   # motörhead

Q: How do I get the application exit code from a Windows command line? A:

I have been using this script since DR-DOS, and of course it has changed somewhat since then.

@ECHO OFF
CLS
IF "%1" == "" GOTO :ERRORINPUT
SET ERROLV_TEST=%*

ECHO Testing Errorlevels:
ECHO ────────────────────
ECHO ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
ECHO %ERROLV_TEST%
ECHO ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
ECHO/
%ERROLV_TEST%
FOR /L %%x in (255,-1,0) do if errorlevel %%x ECHO Error Code is: %%x
ECHO/
ECHO/
PAUSE
GOTO :END

:ERRORINPUT
REM Beep with BEL
ECHO • 
ECHO Error:   No parameters given
ECHO Usage:   ERRORLVL.CMD {command}
ECHO Example: ERRORLVL START /WAIT REGSVR32.EXE /S BROKEN.DLL
ECHO/
PAUSE
GOTO :END

:END
EXIT /B

EDIT: Here is another good explanation of ERRORLEVELS: Errorlevel and Exit codes

Q: Find an explicit criterion about a specific class of integer sequences expressed by a recursive predicate A:

As a matter of fact, it is for compression. I was hoping that a tree sequence could be specified by a sequence of branching operations that generate it. It's true that a tree sequence of length n will require n-1 branching operations to be specified, so it seems that there is little room for compression. However, tree sequences are not arbitrary sequences. They have some structure, which I hope to understand and exploit. Understanding the branching operations is just an angle to understand the structure of a tree sequence.

Is this a hopeless task?

Q: Is it possible to do fuzzy match merge with pandas? A:

There is a package called fuzzy_pandas that can use levenshtein, jaro, metaphone and bilenco methods, with some great examples.

import pandas as pd
import fuzzy_pandas as fpd

df1 = pd.DataFrame(
    {'Key': ['Apple', 'Banana', 'Orange', 'Strawberry']})
df2 = pd.DataFrame(
    {'Key': ['Aple', 'Mango', 'Orag', 'Straw', 'Bannanna', 'Berry']})

results = fpd.fuzzy_merge(
    df1,
    df2,
    left_on='Key',
    right_on='Key',
    method='levenshtein',
    threshold=0.6)

results.head()

  Key    Key
0 Apple  Aple
1 Banana Bannanna
2 Orange Orag
